answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce stake and complete randomly assigned tasks checked by independent reviewers before receiving valuable work. A sable account may enter through an inlet, but copying its software does not copy its stake or verified history. Each fake identity must lock more capital and repeat the checks; if caught cheating, it loses the stake. In an orchard of agents, Sybil attacks therefore cost money per identity and risk forfeiture.
